They make an impact in their communities providing advice and implementing recommendations in a purpose-driven career with opportunities for unlimited income potential, independence, and growth.
 People from various professional and educational backgrounds have found success in the advisor career at Sunlife. That’s because being a successful advisor is not just about what’s on your resume. It’s about who you are as a person.
 Are you someone who loves talking to people and comfortable providing advice?
 Are you disciplined and motivated?
 Do you value your independence?
 Do you love learning and developing new skills?
 If this sounds like you, let’s talk!
 What’s in it for you?
 Unlimited earning potential with compensation that is tied to your achievements and provides an ongoing stream of income.
 “Earn while you learn” monthly bonuses to provide financial stability as you develop your skills in a new career.
 A purpose-driven career helping people in your community become more financially secure. 
 The independence and flexibility to build your work around the important things in your life.

 A culture that celebrates excellence and inclusivity.

 Prepare and execute strategies to attract and connect with new Clients.
 Conduct meetings with prospective and existing Clients.
 Review their current financial state and gather information about their future goals.
 Build a financial roadmap to help them achieve these goals.
 Recommend and implement suitable insurance and investment products that align with this financial roadmap.
 Continue to meet with Clients to ensure their plan stays up to date as their life situation changes (family, career, housing, debts, etc.)

 Business development skills.

At Hydro Ottawa, we power the lives of the people in the communities we serve.  
 We are seeking a Grid Technology Specialist who enjoys hands-on work with the support of a collaborative team; a problem solver who always puts safety first. Without you, we’d be in the dark.  
 JOB SUMMARY 
 The Grid Technology Specialist is responsible for the administration, design, development, implementation, and maintenance of multiple Class A and Class B Operations Smart Grid Technology Systems. This includes managing distribution asset information and planning the business process integration of GIS and other software based operational systems with other corporate enterprise applications. The Grid Technology Specialist is also responsible for the research, evaluation and recommendation of solutions required for the strategic implementation of all distribution Smart Grid systems for the corporation. 
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The essential responsibilities of the job include but are not limited to the following:
 Responsible for the administration of Class A systems include the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, the Distribution Management System (DMS), the Outage Management System (OMS), and P-Tech system, as well as Class B systems including the Geographic Information System (GIS) and other systems such as PI , CYME, 4Command, and Computer-Assisted Drafting (CAD).
 Responsible for the design, configuration, provisioning, commissioning, and administration of the Analog, Status and Control points within the SCADA application.
 Responsible for the management, configuration and administration of critical communication components within SCADA, including Channels, Channel Groups, RTUs, Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol (ICCP) connections, and PI connections.
 Responsible for the configuration and administration of alarming in SCADA in accordance with established standards and requirements.
 Responsible for the design, creation and management of all single line diagrams and displays in SCADA.
 Coordinate with IESO, Hydro One, and City of Ottawa Light Rail Transit for ICCP point configuration, commissioning, and maintenance.
 Coordinate  with outside Operations staff including Stations Technicians and Stations Supervisors for integration and commissioning of new field devices.
 Evaluate and test field devices with Distribution Assets, Stations, and Operations groups.
 Responsible for SCADA Incident Response including reporting anomalous or suspicious behaviour, triaging issues and concerns, and take appropriate action as per Hydro Ottawa policies and procedures and escalating to appropriate parties (cybersecurity team, vendor) when necessary.
 First responder to Class A and Class B Grid Technology systems performing triage, investigating, and resolving issues. When required, engaging other groups, coordinating their actions, and ensuring resolutions are reached in a timely manner.
 Researches and evaluates Operations Smart Grid Technology systems software including Class A (SCADA/DMS/OMS/P-Tech), Class B (GIS/PI), other systems (4Command/CYME/CAD), and makes recommendations for their use.
 Administer SCADA (including ICCP) and DMS Oracle databases in the Training and Development System, pre-production, and production environments.
 Configure and maintain OMS and GIS Oracle databases in both development and production environments.
 Administer, configure, and maintain proprietary PI database in the production environment 
 Identify specifications, create fields and tables, and develop/generate reports for databases in Oracle and Access using MS SQL or other platforms for Operations asset records, including distribution circuits, poles, streetlights, manholes, switches, stations, etc.
 Liaise with IT DMI group on the management of Operations electronic databases used by GIS, OMS, SCADA, and other applications.
 Develop criteria and specifications for the proper management of asset data maintained by Operations.
 Design, develop and lead patching of Class A, Class B, and other systems impacting Grid Technology.
 Lead activities for the collection and implementation of Operations field data.
 Automation of system reports and tasks through scripting and software tools.
 Contribute as a member of the Grid Technology team for developing the overall corporate strategy for Operations software applications used in the management of Hydro Ottawa’s distribution grid.
 Develop and maintain documentation for Smart Grid Technology standards and procedures.
 Develop and maintain contacts with suppliers and users, including municipalities and external agencies.
 Assist with the negotiation of Operations Smart Grid Technology supply and support contracts, and to resolve issues as they arise.
 Develop Request for Proposal documents for the provisions of vendor services, evaluates proposals, assists with the negotiation of details, and makes recommendations for implementation.
 Undertake business process administrator responsibility for all Operations Smart Grid technology related software and hardware.
 Provide business process support and liaises with users of Smart Grid Technology solutions and recommends methods of meeting these needs.
 Lead or participate in the development and deployment of business processes and related Operations technologies.
 Provide input to the Grid Technology budget process and generates purchase requisitions.
 Coordinate activities for the conversion of hard copy records to an electronic format.
 Develop and provide training sessions for staff on the use of Operations software applications.
 Develop and deliver oral presentations.
 Ensure that all corporate policies are followed.
 Perform other related duties as assigned.
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 
 A university degree or college diploma in a related technical discipline. 
 Working knowledge of Oracle SQL, Visual Basic / C, Dot Net (.net ) programming languages or equivalent programming languages  including a strong knowledge of Access. 
 Working knowledge of geospatial theories and terminologies.  
 Working knowledge of Microstation and/or AutoCAD digital mapping concepts. 
 Working knowledge of electrical distribution system theory, terminology, and equipment. 
 Strong computer skills; proficient in the use of office productivity and collaboration tools, preferably G Suite. 
 Experience in the development and maintenance of SCADA, GIS or OMS applications considered an asset. 
 Previous exposure to real time software packages such as historical trending packages and ICCP is considered and asset. 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
 English Essential, both oral and written 
 Bilingual (French and English) is considered an asset. 
 Valid driver’s license - Class G

The Project Coordinator, Architectural Trades supports the planning, procurement, coordination, installation, inspection, and closeout of architectural construction packages for station and associated building areas. 
 Working closely with the Architectural Project Manager, site supervision, design consultants, quality teams, commercial teams, suppliers, and subcontractors, the Project Coordinator helps ensure that architectural work is executed safely, in the correct sequence, and in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, contract requirements, approved samples, applicable codes, and project quality standards. 
 The position focuses specifically on architectural and building-finish scopes, rather than civil works. These may include masonry, façade, drywall and partitions, ceilings, architectural metalwork, doors and hardware, glazing, roofing, waterproofing, cladding, flooring, tiling, painting, millwork, signage, louvers, firestopping, sealants, and other interior and exterior architectural finishes. 
 The salary range for this position is $90,000 CAD - $120,000 CAD, plus additional benefits.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Architectural Planning & Coordination 
 Coordinate architectural construction packages from design development and procurement through installation, inspection, deficiency correction, and final turnover.
 Review architectural drawings, reflected ceiling plans, room data sheets, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, method statements, and installation details. 
 Confirm that subcontractor shop drawings and technical submittals are coordinated with the latest approved design information before materials are released for fabrication or installation. 
 Identify discrepancies, missing information, constructability concerns, dimensional conflicts, and interface issues affecting architectural work. 
 Prepare, submit, track, and close Requests for Information relating to architectural design, finishes, materials, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, and installation requirements. 
 Coordinate architectural requirements with structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, communications, security, vertical transportation, and other interfacing disciplines. 
 Work with design and field teams to confirm wall openings, embeds, sleeves, access panels, equipment clearances, ceiling coordination, service penetrations, backing, supports, and finishing requirements. 
 Support the preparation of architectural work plans, look-ahead schedules, installation sequences, access requirements, logistics arrangements, and area-release plans. 
 Coordinate architectural samples, colour selections, material approvals, control samples, first-work inspections, and mock-ups. 
 Maintain architectural trackers for submittals, RFIs, samples, mock-ups, design changes, procurement, installation status, inspections, deficiencies, and closeout documentation. 
 Procurement, Construction, and Field Coordination 
 Assist in defining architectural subcontractor scopes of work and identifying scope gaps, exclusions, overlaps, and trade interfaces. 
 Support the preparation and review of bid packages, technical comparisons, scope clarifications, supplier proposals, subcontractor submissions, and procurement recommendations. 
 Coordinate with procurement teams, suppliers, fabricators, and architectural subcontractors to monitor material approvals, fabrication activities, delivery dates, storage requirements, and installation readiness. 
 Track long-lead architectural materials and equipment, including doors and hardware, glazing systems, cladding, specialty finishes, ceiling systems, architectural metalwork, millwork, signage, and custom-fabricated components. 
 Confirm that materials delivered to site correspond with approved submittals, samples, finishes, colours, quantities, and project requirements. 
 Monitor architectural activities in the field and coordinate with site supervisors and subcontractors to maintain the required work sequence and planned production. 
 Verify that work areas are ready before architectural subcontractors mobilize, including access, preceding-work completion, environmental conditions, dimensions, temporary services, material storage, and protection requirements. 
 Coordinate access, hoisting, work zones, laydown areas, temporary protection, material handling, and interfaces between architectural subcontractors operating in shared areas. 
 Participate in daily coordination meetings, weekly subcontractor meetings, look-ahead planning sessions, design reviews, quality meetings, and progress meetings. 
 Monitor architectural subcontractor manpower, productivity, work fronts, constraints, and scheduled completion dates. 
 Identify and escalate potential delays, incomplete prerequisites, design constraints, procurement risks, coordination conflicts, and quality concerns. 
 Support the development and implementation of practical mitigation and recovery measures. 
 Ensure architectural activities are carried out in compliance with project health and safety requirements, environmental requirements, approved work plans, and site procedures. 
 Quality, Compliance, and Closeout 
 Support quality assurance and quality control activities for architectural work. 
 Verify that architectural installations comply with approved drawings, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, manufacturer requirements, inspection and test plans, applicable codes, and project standards. 
 Coordinate inspections with subcontractors, site supervision, quality personnel, consultants, designers, authorities, and other stakeholders, as applicable. 
 Prepare and maintain inspection requests, checklists, deficiency lists, non-conformance records, corrective-action records, and associated quality documentation. 
 Monitor workmanship, alignment, tolerances, finishes, colour consistency, joint treatment, transitions, interfaces, protection, and final appearance. 
 Confirm that concealed architectural work and interfacing conditions are inspected before walls, ceilings, cladding systems, or other finishes are closed. 
 Coordinate testing and specialist inspections related to architectural systems, where required, including water penetration, adhesion, pull testing, sealant, firestopping, door operation, hardware functionality, and other specified performance requirements. 
 Manage architectural deficiencies from initial identification through correction, reinspection, acceptance, and closure. 
 Coordinate room-by-room, area-by-area, or system-based inspections and turnover activities. 
 Support the preparation of as-built drawings, warranties, maintenance information, attic stock records, spare-material inventories, operation and maintenance manuals, training records, product data, certificates, and turnover packages. 
 Confirm that architectural closeout documentation is complete, accurate, properly organized, and submitted in accordance with project requirements. 
 Support final cleaning, protection removal, touch-ups, finish repairs, and the presentation of completed areas for inspection and handover. 
 Progress Reporting, Cost Control, and Change Management 
 Track architectural progress by trade, area, level, work package, or construction zone. 
 Maintain accurate records of completed quantities, planned versus actual progress, outstanding work, constraints, deficiencies, and forecast completion dates. 
 Prepare weekly and monthly architectural progress reports, dashboards, photographs, trackers, and management updates. 
 Assist with schedule reviews and short-term planning for architectural packages, including three-week, six-week, and other project-specific look-ahead schedules. 
 Support quantity tracking, installed-progress measurement, subcontractor progress reviews, and payment-assessment processes. 
 Review subcontractor progress claims against actual work completed, accepted materials, approved changes, deficiencies, and supporting records. 
 Maintain records supporting architectural changes, including instructions, RFIs, site conditions, labour records, material records, photographs, quotations, and schedule impacts. 
 Assist in identifying potential changes, scope growth, rework, design development, and out-of-sequence work. 
 Support the review of subcontractor quotations and change-order documentation for completeness and alignment with the defined architectural scope. 
 Assist with cost forecasting, commitment tracking, accruals, quantity reconciliation, and architectural package cost reporting. 
 Monitor material waste, rework, damage, productivity, and subcontractor performance, and support corrective measures where needed. 
 Maintain accurate daily and weekly records to support progress verification, commercial discussions, schedule analysis, and dispute avoidance. 
 Identify trends, recurring constraints, and opportunities to improve architectural coordination, procurement, installation, inspection, and turnover processes.
College diploma or bachelor's degree (preferred) in Architecture, Architectural Technology, Construction Management, Building Science, Engineering Technology, or another construction-related discipline.
 Two to three years of experience in project coordination, construction coordination, architectural construction, building finishes, or a related construction environment. 
 Experience reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, shop drawings, material submissions, samples, and finish schedules. 
 Experience coordinating subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, and field activities.

 Strong attention to detail, particularly regarding finishes, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, approved materials, and documentation status. 
 Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
 Ability to communicate professionally with project managers, superintendents, subcontractors, architects, consultants, suppliers, quality personnel, and client representatives. 
 Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary project team while maintaining ownership of assigned actions. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify practical solutions to architectural coordination and field-installation issues. 
 Ability to spend time in active construction areas and verify progress and conditions directly in the field.

 Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams. 
 Ability to develop and maintain progress trackers, submittal logs, RFI logs, procurement schedules, deficiency lists, quantity records, and reporting tools in Excel. 
 Ability to review, mark up, compare, and organize architectural drawings and technical documents electronically.

At Asana, security is foundational to our mission of helping teams work together effortlessly. Our security team protects Asana's employees, users, and customers by proactively addressing threats, ensuring compliance, and fostering a culture of security throughout our product and operations.
 As the Security Risk Engineer, you will own Asana's internal security risk management program end-to-end. This is a senior role for someone who goes beyond frameworks and checklists — you will engineer the quantitative and automated foundations that let Asana continuously measure and make confident decisions about security risk. You'll build the systems and processes that make risk scalable, not just the policies that describe it, and serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership.
 This role is based in our Vancouver, BC office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements
 What you'll achieve 
 Own Asana's security risk management program: Design and continuously mature a quantitative risk framework — including risk scoring methodologies, likelihood and impact modeling, and risk appetite thresholds — that enables consistent, data-driven risk decisions across the organization.
 Build and maintain a living risk register: Own Asana's central security risk register, developing KRIs, tracking trends over time, and driving accountability for risk treatment and remediation with business and technical owners.
 Automate risk identification and monitoring: Design and implement automated data pipelines and integrations that continuously surface security risks — pulling signals from vulnerability scanners, cloud security tooling, SIEMs, and third-party risk sources — so Asana's risk posture is always current and not dependent on manual review cycles.

 Partner cross-functionally on risk: Act as the primary security risk partner to Legal, Privacy, Finance, and Engineering. Influence security investment decisions and build a culture of risk awareness across the company.

 7+ years of experience in information security with a strong focus on security risk management and GRC.
 Demonstrated experience building or leading a security risk management program — not just contributing to one.
 Hands-on experience with quantitative risk methodologies such as FAIR, risk scoring models, or statistical risk analysis. You back up risk ratings with numbers, not just color codes.
 Hands-on experience scripting or building automation to integrate security tooling, build data pipelines, or automate risk monitoring — you've built things, not just directed others to build them.Deep knowledge of security frameworks including NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-30, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and FedRAMP.
 Proven ability to develop risk metrics, KRIs, and executive-level reporting that drives decision-making.
 Strong understanding of cloud environments and SaaS architecture — enough to have credible risk conversations with technical teams.
 Excellent communicator who can translate technical risk findings for both engineering teams and C-suite stakeholders.
 Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity and decision-making.

Why this role?

 We're doing $50M+ a year and scaling to $100M+ , and we want one person who owns the money so we don't run into problems as we double the business.  Own the company's money: cash, books, payments, projections and financial planning, so the CEO always knows where cash and profit stand today and where they are heading + improving terms, cash conversion cycle etc. Success is clear, accurate projections on cash flow, subscriptions and the cash conversion cycle so there are no surprises, books closed on time every month, and every payment and filing right and on time.  Who are we?
 We are a profitable DTC brand selling premium pet products.  Better Everyday: make the close, the cash forecast, payments and tax filing a bit faster and cleaner every month, and fix the root cause of every payment or booking error.
 Speed Is King: have the 13-week cash flow current before our Monday leadership meeting, pay bills and contractors on time, close the books on schedule, and flag a cash risk or overrun the week it shows up.
 Work Smart: automate finance work so a part-time role covers the whole function.  Overdeliver: bring the CEO the decision the numbers point to, not just the numbers, and find savings and cash-timing wins before being asked.

 Outcomes (what success looks like)

 Project subscriptions, subscription cohorts and the cash conversion cycle, and flag anything moving against plan the week it shows up.

 Grow our credit lines and set up an asset-based lending facility so the next two quarters of POs are always funded.

 Fluent in English

 À propos de & Whitney Canada 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.
 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. 
 Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.
 Pourquoi rejoindre l’équipe des Technologies Numériques de Pratt & Whitney Canada ? 
 Nous sommes en pleine transformation numérique, redéfinissant notre manière de travailler, optimisant nos opérations et transformant nos produits et services pour améliorer les expériences des employés et des clients.
 En tant que membre de notre équipe de Technologie Numérique, vous contribuerez à façonner l’avenir en travaillant avec des outils avancés, en automatisant les processus et en innovant dans toutes les fonctions de l’entreprise.
 Notre organisation mondiale est déterminée à cultiver une équipe autonome et compétente afin d’apporter des solutions avancées et des capacités numériques à la pointe de la technologie à nos clients.
 Sommaire du poste 
 L’organisation Cybersécurité de RTX Pratt & Whitney est à la recherche d’un(e) leader expérimenté(e) et hautement motivé(e) en cybersécurité et conformité (Cybersecurity & Compliance Leader – CCL) pour agir à titre de partenaire stratégique auprès de domaines d’affaires assignés. Ce rôle se situe à l’intersection des risques cyber, de la conformité et des opérations d’affaires, en veillant à ce que les priorités de cybersécurité de l’entreprise soient comprises, adoptées et mises en œuvre au sein des unités d’affaires, tout en offrant une visibilité à la direction sur le niveau de risque local.
 Le ou la CCL agit à titre de conseiller(ère) de confiance, de traducteur(trice) des risques et de liaison avec les unités d’affaires. Il ou elle est responsable d’aligner les exigences en cybersécurité et en conformité avec les objectifs d’affaires, de piloter la gouvernance des risques et d’assurer la préparation aux exigences réglementaires internes et externes. Ce rôle contribue de façon clé à l’assurance de mission cyber de Pratt & Whitney ainsi qu’à la posture globale de cybersécurité de l’entreprise.
 Les CCL ne sont pas des opérateurs — ils assurent la responsabilisation des risques, la clarté et l’action au sein des unités d’affaires, afin que la cybersécurité soutienne la réussite des missions, la continuité des opérations et la confiance des clients.
 Ce rôle sera également responsable de supporter un programme de contrôles DT, en partenariat avec Enterprise Services, afin de valider de façon indépendante le travail effectué par la première ligne de défense.
 Principes directeurs de l’équipe 
 L’entreprise d’abord, la cybersécurité toujours : chaque interaction débute par les résultats d’affaires et se conclut par une mise en œuvre sécurisée.
 Standardiser lorsque possible, adapter lorsque nécessaire : la cohérence favorise l’efficacité; la flexibilité assure la pertinence.
 Proactivité avant réactivité : privilégier l’anticipation et l’alignement précoce plutôt que les interventions de dernière minute.
 Une seule équipe, plusieurs voix : maintenir l’unité à travers le CMS tout en respectant les réalités propres à chaque unité d’affaires.

 Leadership en matière de cybersécurité et de risques de conformité
 Agir à titre de personne responsable et de référence auprès des secteurs d’affaires pour le suivi de la posture en matière de cybersécurité et de risques de conformité pour les contrôles des technologies numériques (Digital Controls).
 Contribuer à fournir une vision intégrée des risques couvrant les environnements TI, TO, infonuagiques, d’ingénierie, les fournisseurs ainsi que les exigences réglementaires.
 Veiller à ce que les décisions liées aux risques soient prises en charge, dotées des ressources nécessaires et priorisées par les secteurs d’affaires.

 Intégrer les considérations liées aux contrôles des technologies numériques dans les stratégies d’affaires, les programmes et les initiatives majeures, notamment la modernisation, les systèmes d’ingénierie et les opérations manufacturières.
 Représenter les besoins des secteurs d’affaires auprès des équipes de cybersécurité, de conformité et de technologies numériques afin d’assurer leur alignement et leur priorisation.
 Traduire la stratégie, les normes et les feuilles de route de l’entreprise en matière de cybersécurité en plans d’action concrets et adaptés aux besoins des secteurs d’affaires.
 Gouvernance, responsabilisation et revues des risques
 Diriger les forums de gouvernance des contrôles des technologies numériques destinés aux secteurs d’affaires, notamment les revues de risques, les suivis de programmes et les discussions liées à la préparation à la conformité.
 Assurer la traçabilité et le suivi des mesures d’atténuation, des décisions de financement et de l’acceptation des risques.
 Fournir aux leaders des informations claires, concises et concrètes sur la posture des contrôles des technologies numériques, les écarts identifiés et les progrès réalisés.
 Préparation et maintien de la conformité
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes internes et externes afin de contribuer au maintien de la préparation aux audits selon les cadres réglementaires applicables, notamment la CMMC, les exigences des clients gouvernementaux et les politiques de RTX.

 Communication, gestion du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes
 Communiquer les risques liés à la cybersécurité, les politiques et les changements de façon claire, adaptée et accessible aux secteurs d’affaires.
 Mobiliser les leaders et les équipes en développant des relations solides et des partenariats efficaces entre les différentes fonctions.
 Favoriser la sensibilisation et l’adoption d’une culture axée sur les comportements sécuritaires et le respect des obligations de conformité.
 Mesure de la performance et amélioration continue
 Contribuer à définir et à faire connaître les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), les mesures et les indicateurs liés à la posture des contrôles des technologies numériques, en cohérence avec les modèles de l’entreprise.
 Identifier les tendances systémiques et les occasions d’amélioration, et collaborer avec les équipes techniques afin de contribuer à l’élaboration de solutions.
 Promouvoir l’optimisation, l’innovation et les principes CORE afin de soutenir l’excellence opérationnelle.
 Principes CORE : Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en s’appuyant sur les principes RTX CORE ( Customer Oriented Results and Excellence ) afin de favoriser l’innovation et l’efficacité opérationnelle.

POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Manager, Quality Assurance, the Quality Assurance Engineer will be responsible for delivering quality software for the Trulioo SaaS platform. This role involves designing and executing manual and automated tests across UI, API, and database layers, and integrating them into CI/CD pipelines.

This is a full-time, permanent position based out of our Vancouver office, working on a hybrid model (3 days per week in-office).

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Execute the strategic vision using technologies required to ensure the delivery of quality software for the Trulioo SaaS platform.

 - Contribute to bug tracking, test prioritization, test automation, and release validation.

 - Influence design by reviewing requirements, behaviour specifications, and design documents to begin test development early and uncover risks before implementation.

 - Develop and document full-stack test strategies, design test cases, and conduct manual and automated testing across platforms and technology layers, including UI, API, database, Android, and iOS.

 - Work with QA engineers across engineering disciplines to apply a test-automation-first strategy and integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.

 - Mentor and coach junior engineers on the team.

 - Assist the team in creating and executing basic performance, load, and stress test scenarios with tools such as k6.

 - Run baseline performance tests and create documentation to capture key metrics such as response times, throughput, and error rates with tools such as Grafana.

 - Use generative AI development tools such as Codex and Cursor to accelerate test design, automation development, debugging, defect investigation, and technical documentation.

 - Design, build, and integrate custom AI tools and agents into internal Quality Engineering workflows.

 - Build integrations using Model Context Protocol (MCP), APIs, tool calling, and existing engineering systems.

 - Apply prompt-engineering techniques to produce accurate, reusable, and maintainable AI-assisted workflows.

 - Review and validate AI-generated code, test cases, and technical analysis to ensure accuracy, security, maintainability, and alignment with engineering standards.

 - Evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify practical opportunities to improve product quality and engineering productivity.

 - Follow security, privacy, and responsible-use practices when using AI tools with source code, customer information, or personally identifiable information.

 - Design, build, and integrate custom AI tools and agents into internal workflows while serving as a technical subject matter expert on emerging AI technologies.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience developing automated tests using test automation frameworks at the API and UI layers.

 - 5+ years of experience with UI and API testing frameworks and tools such as Cypress, Selenium, Playwright, Postman, RestAssured, or similar.

 - Proven experience in at least one scripting or programming language, such as C#, Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or similar.

 - Solid technical understanding of SaaS platforms, REST APIs, web applications, databases, and distributed systems.

 - Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.

 - Introductory experience with industry tools such as k6,JMeter, Locust, or Postman performance testing.

 - Basic understanding of APIs and how to test endpoints under simulated user load.

 - Familiarity with application monitoring tools (e.g.,Grafana, Datadog, New Relic) to observe system health during runs.

 - Practical experience using generative AI development tools such as Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar tools in software development or Quality Engineering workflows.

 - Experience designing prompts and reusable instructions for code generation, test creation, debugging, requirements analysis, or technical documentation.

 - Experience building or integrating AI agents, AI-assisted automation, or custom internal AI tools.

 - Familiarity with MCP, API-based integrations, tool calling, or connecting AI tools to internal systems and development workflows.

 - Ability to critically review and validate AI-generated code, test cases, and recommendations.

 - Understanding of security, privacy, access-control, and data-handling considerations when adopting AI tools in an enterprise environment.

 - A Bachelor of Science degree in computer science, engineering, or another STEM field, or a comparable combination of education, training, and experience.
   
   

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience testing mobile platforms, including Android and iOS.

 - Experience delivering quality products in Agile teams using technologies such as AWS Device Farm, microservices, Docker, and AWS.

 - Experience building internal tools and quality dashboards.

 - Experience creating AI agents or workflows that support test generation, requirements analysis, defect triage, failure analysis, test-data creation, or release validation.

 - Experience developing MCP servers or integrating MCP-compatible tools with engineering platforms.

 - Experience evaluating AI-assisted workflows for accuracy, consistency, security, latency, cost, and operational value.

 - Experience establishing standards or best practices for the responsible use of generative AI in engineering teams.

 - Experience with BDD and TDD practices.

 À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.
 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.
 Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe? 
 Êtes-vous prêt à concevoir des logiciels qui propulsent l’avenir de l’aviation? Joignez-vous à nous à titre d’ingénieur en conception de logiciels de systèmes de commande et faites partie d’une équipe qui développe des logiciels de systèmes de commande de pointe et essentiels à la sécurité pour les moteurs d’aéronefs. 
 Dans le cadre de ce poste, vous travaillerez à toutes les étapes du cycle de vie DO-178, de la capture des exigences et de la conception jusqu’à la vérification et à la certification. Vous collaborerez avec nos équipes d’ingénierie, nos fournisseurs, nos clients et nos organisations d’essais afin de développer et de soutenir des produits nouveaux et en service. Si vous êtes animé par l’innovation, la collaboration et la passion de voir votre travail prendre son envol, ce poste est pour vous!
 Le poste est basé dans l’un de nos établissements de Mississauga , en Ontario, ou de Longueuil , au Québec. Il s’agit d’un poste entièrement en présentiel, du lundi au vendredi.
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 Développer l’architecture logicielle, les exigences et le code des logiciels de systèmes de commande de moteurs d’aéronefs à l’aide de la conception basée sur des modèles, ainsi que des langages Assembly, Ada, C/C++ et autres langages de programmation.
 Effectuer des revues, des analyses et des essais approfondis des systèmes logiciels en collaboration avec notre équipe d’ingénierie mondiale.
 Créer et examiner les livrables de certification, soutenir les audits SOI et veiller à ce que nos logiciels respectent les normes les plus élevées de l’industrie et soient conformes à la norme DO-178.
 Soutenir les activités d’essais logiciels dans des environnements de simulation, sur des bancs d’essai, dans des cellules d’essai et lors d’essais en vol.
 Être un agent de changement en favorisant l’amélioration des processus et en nous aidant à repousser les limites de l’automatisation.

 Baccalauréat en génie ou en informatique.
 Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans les domaines des systèmes de commande, des systèmes embarqués essentiels à la sécurité, de l’avionique ou des turbines à gaz.
 Connaissance des systèmes de propulsion, des capteurs, des actionneurs et des interfaces avec l’aéronef.
 Expérience avec la norme DO-178 ou des normes similaires.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.
 Esprit de collaboration et capacité à s’épanouir dans un environnement axé sur le travail d’équipe.
 Esprit proactif et capacité d’adaptation, avec une aptitude à relever des défis et à trouver des solutions créatives.
 Excellentes compétences en organisation et en gestion du temps.

 Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada

 Job Title: Control Systems Software Design Engineer
 About Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 An Employer of Choice 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada was named one of Canada’s Best Employers for 2026 by Forbes, marking the 11th consecutive year the company has earned this recognition. Pratt & Whitney Canada also ranked #1 employer in the aerospace and defense industry in the country. In addition, our headquarters continues to be recognized among the top employers in the Montreal region. Together, these distinctions reinforce our reputation as an employer of choice in Montreal, across Canada, and around the world.
 Why join our team? 
 Are you ready to design software that powers the future of flight? Join us as a Control Systems Software Design Engineer and be part of a team developing cutting-edge, safety-critical control system software for aircraft engines. 
 In this role, you’ll work across the DO-178 lifecycle, from requirements capture and design through verification and certification. You’ll collaborate with our engineering teams, suppliers, customers, and test organizations to develop and support both new and in-service products. If you’re driven by innovation, collaboration, and the thrill of seeing your work take to the skies, this is the role for you!
 The position is based at either our Mississauga , Ontario, or Longueuil , Quebec, locations. This position is fully on-site, Monday through Friday.
 Develop aircraft engine control system software architecture, requirements, and code using model-based design, Assembly, Ada, C/C++, and other programming languages.
 Perform in-depth reviews, analysis, and testing of software systems in collaboration with our global engineering team.
 Create and review certification artifacts, support SOI audits, and ensure our software meets the highest industry standards and complies with DO-178.
 Support software testing activities in simulations, test benches, test cells, and flight tests.
 Be a change agent by driving process improvements and helping us push the boundaries of automation.

About Tailscale 
 About the Role 
 We are seeking a Product Manager to own Tailscale's Identity ecosystem — the bridge between our "Zero Trust" networking philosophy and the existing identity infrastructure our customers already rely on. Identity is the foundation of access control in Tailscale; if a user cannot authenticate or authorize correctly, the network cannot be secure. In this role, you will bridge the gap between complex security protocols (OIDC, SAML, SCIM) and a seamless, "it just works" user experience.
 The Identity portfolio covers the end-to-end lifecycle of a user and device within the tailnet:
 Authentication: Integrating with external Identity Providers (IdPs) so users can log in using the credentials they already have (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, etc.).
 Authorization: Defining how roles, groups, and attributes translate into granular network access policies.
 Lifecycle Management: Automating the onboarding, offboarding, and synchronization (SCIM) of users and devices as they change roles or leave organizations.
 These capabilities are where Tailscale meets the customer's existing security stack. Nearly every enterprise deployment begins with an identity integration, grows through complex multi-IdP setups, and increasingly depends on automated lifecycle management for production security.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Tailscale's Identity portfolio: workload and agent identity, SSO integrations, Directory Sync (SCIM), access controls and policy, user management.
 Own the operator experience for admins: How IT and security teams configure identity providers, audit authentication events, and manage user, workload, and agent access policies at scale, across the admin console, API, and clients.
 Build a best-in-class authentication experience for end-users: Save our users time and money by making every auth flow fast, secure, and intuitive.
 Partner closely across engineering, product, and design org to ensure Tailscale’s identity service meets the needs of the broader organization and integrates tightly with other platform components.
 Build systematic customer insight across the full spread of Tailscale users, from a homelab operator exposing a media server through Funnel to a regulated enterprise routing traffic across multi-region datacenters.
 Turn customer signal, support patterns, cross-product requests, and competitive dynamics into roadmap priorities
 What We Are Looking For 
 4–7 years in product management, with direct ownership of an identity product or platform.
 Strong technical fluency in identity protocols: Comfortable engaging engineers as a peer on OIDC, SAML, SCIM, WebAuthn, and OAuth flows.
 Experience shipping products for developer or security-focused audiences: You understand the friction points of modern IAM and know how to build tools that admins and developers actually enjoy using.
 Demonstrated ability to own a product area end to end: Strategy, roadmap, execution, and the customer relationships that keep you honest.
 Operational mindset: You understand that for an identity product, downtime or misconfiguration isn't just a bug—it’s a security event.
 Nice to Have 
 Hands-on experience with Tailscale at work or home.
 Background working with specific Identity Providers (Okta, Azure Entra ID/Active Directory, Google Workspace) or Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) architectures.
 Experience with cloud-native identity concepts: service mesh, workload identity federation
 Public technical writing, conference talks, or open-source contributions in the security or identity space.

Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.
 CAN Pay Range
 $237,180 — $296,140 CAD 
 What We Offer 
 A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).
 Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities.

About Moment Energy 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Senior Reliability Engineer to help ensure the long-term reliability, durability, and performance of Moment Energy's battery energy storage systems (BESS). In this role, you will develop reliability models, translate field and simulated operating conditions into mission profiles, and help predict product life and identify potential failure mechanisms. You will also support failure analysis investigations and prepare technical reliability reports that demonstrate product performance to our customers.
 This is an opportunity to contribute to the development and improvement of our reliability engineering practices as we scale our second-life battery technology. You will work closely with engineering, testing, and product development teams to turn operating data into actionable engineering insights and help improve confidence in our products.
 Responsibilities and Duties 
 Develop and apply reliability methodologies to assess product durability, expected service life, and performance across Moment Energy's battery energy storage systems.
